sources.entry: Nudge - Free, open-source window manager with keyboard shortcuts and drag-to-edge snapping.

summary.one_liner: Nudge is a free, open-source macOS window manager that snaps, resizes and moves windows using keyboard shortcuts and drag-to-edge gestures.
summary.what_it_does: Nudge is a menu bar app for macOS that repositions and resizes the focused window. It provides 19 keyboard-shortcut actions covering left, right, top and bottom halves, four corner quarters, left/center/right thirds, left and center and right two-thirds, maximize, center, restore, and moving a window to the next or previous display. Dragging a window to a screen edge or corner snaps it into place. All default shortcuts can be remapped in the Settings panel under Shortcuts. The README's comparison table positions it against Magnet and Rectangle, claiming a sub-1MB app size and no App Store requirement.
use_cases: snap a window to half or quarter of the screen
tile windows side by side on mac
move a window to another monitor with a shortcut
free replacement for paid window snapping apps
maximize or center a window quickly
how_to_run: open Nudge.xcodeproj, then press Cmd+R to build and run
Grant Accessibility permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility on first launch
notable: 19 default keyboard shortcuts for halves, quarters, thirds, maximize, center and display moves
Signed and notarized DMG download, also installable via Homebrew
Menu bar app with remappable shortcuts in Settings
Compared directly against Magnet and Rectangle in the README
caveats: Building from source needs Xcode 14+ and xcodegen
Needs Accessibility permission granted on first launch
README does not state a version number or recent maintenance activity
